fr:mainmatter.html:p: A monoidal category is left closed if for each Y \in C, the functor - \otimes Y : C \to C has a right adjoint {Y} \multimap _L {-} : C \to C forming the left internal-hom out of Y.
That is, for all X,Y,Z, there is a natural isomorphism C[X \otimes Y , Z] \cong C[ X , [Y , Z]]

There is an obvious right-handed variant {Y} \multimap _R {-} that is right adjoint to Y \otimes -. Note: this is likely better denoted with a flipped symbol, but I don't yet know if I can include it in Forester.
If C is both right and left closed, the monoidal category is simply called closed (or perhaps biclosed).
A monoidal category is a category C equipped with the following structure and axioms:

html:ol.html:li: a functor C\times C\xrightarrow {\otimes }C called the tensor product;
an object I\in C called the tensor unit;
a natural isomorphism {\mathopen {}\left (x\otimes y\right )\mathclose {}}\otimes z \xrightarrow {\alpha _{x,y,z}} x\otimes {\mathopen {}\left (y\otimes z\right )\mathclose {}} called the associator;
a natural isomorphism I\otimes x \xrightarrow {\lambda _{x}}x called the left unitor;
a natural isomorphism x\otimes I \xrightarrow {\rho _{x}}x called the right unitor;
